sports.h3: Alcaraz crushes Paul, Tiafoe topples Medvedev on US Open Sunday
sports.summary: Carlos Alcaraz beat Tommy Paul 6-4 6-3 6-4 to reach a sixth straight US Open quarter-final on Sunday 6 September, while Frances Tiafoe knocked out seventh seed Daniil Medvedev to set up an all-American last-eight tie with Alex Michelsen.
body: Defending champion Carlos Alcaraz needed two hours and 20 minutes on Arthur Ashe Stadium on Sunday 6 September to beat 20th seed Tommy Paul 6-4 6-3 6-4. In his first event in four months after a wrist injury, the Spaniard has dropped one set in four rounds, extended his winning run at the majors to 18 matches and leads Paul 7-2 head-to-head.

On Louis Armstrong Stadium, 11th seed Frances Tiafoe produced the upset of the day, beating 2021 champion Daniil Medvedev 7-6(1) 6-4 7-6 for his fourth US Open quarter-final. He faces compatriot Alex Michelsen, who beat Tomas Etcheverry 7-6 6-4 6-4 to reach his first Grand Slam quarter-final at 22. Alcaraz meets the winner of Ben Shelton against Stefanos Tsitsipas.

sports.h3: Sabalenka survives Townsend test, Noskova outlasts Kostyuk
sports.summary: World number one Aryna Sabalenka beat Taylor Townsend 6-4 6-3 in 75 minutes on Sunday to reach a sixth straight US Open quarter-final, where she will meet Wimbledon champion Linda Noskova.
body: Aryna Sabalenka's bid for a third consecutive US Open title survived a scrappy test on Sunday 6 September. The opening set against home favourite Taylor Townsend featured seven breaks of serve in ten games, and Townsend led 3-1 in the second before the top seed won five straight games to close out a 6-4 6-3 win, her 17th in a row in New York.

Sabalenka needs the title, plus an early exit for second seed Elena Rybakina, to keep the number one ranking. Next up is sixth seed Linda Noskova, who outlasted Marta Kostyuk 7-5 5-7 6-4 in two hours and 27 minutes. The bottom half is wide open after Saturday's exits for Madison Keys and Amanda Anisimova, with Jessica Pegula, Anna Kalinskaya and Emma Navarro playing Sunday night.

sports.h3: Antonelli charges from 19th to Monza win, first Italian home winner since 1966
sports.summary: Kimi Antonelli overturned an engine penalty to win the Italian Grand Prix on Sunday 6 September, passing Mercedes teammate George Russell on lap 50 of 53 and stretching his championship lead to 66 points.
body: Kimi Antonelli delivered one of the great Monza drives on Sunday 6 September. Starting 19th after a power unit penalty, the 20-year-old Mercedes driver was sixth by the restart after an early red flag and took the lead from teammate George Russell on lap 18. He pitted for fresh mediums under a Virtual Safety Car while Russell stayed out, then made the winning pass on lap 50.

Antonelli crossed the line 3.857 seconds clear to become the first Italian to win his home grand prix since Ludovico Scarfiotti in 1966. It was his seventh win of the season and stretched his championship lead over Russell to 66 points. Max Verstappen completed the podium for Red Bull, Lando Norris took fourth from Oscar Piastri and Lewis Hamilton salvaged sixth for Ferrari.

sports.h3: Leclerc walks away from huge Parabolica crash as Ferrari's home race unravels
sports.summary: Charles Leclerc crashed heavily at the exit of the Parabolica on lap two of the Italian Grand Prix, bringing out a red flag and leaving Ferrari with a single sixth place at Monza.
body: Ferrari's home weekend collapsed within minutes on Sunday 6 September. Charles Leclerc, running fourth after squeezing teammate Lewis Hamilton onto the gravel at the first chicane, was defending from Oscar Piastri through the Parabolica when the rear of his SF-26 snapped away. The car hit the tyre barrier hard enough to destroy part of it and the race was stopped. Leclerc climbed out unaided.

The stoppage brought a standing restart with George Russell leading from pole-sitter Pierre Gasly. Hamilton, tenth after the Turn 1 incident, recovered to sixth but called the clash with his teammate far too close for comfort. Leclerc said he had fought a loss of rear grip from the first corner. With McLaren fourth and fifth, Ferrari's deficit to the top three was laid bare.

sports.h3: Verstappen takes podium despite straight-line deficit, Gasly fades to seventh
sports.summary: Max Verstappen finished third at Monza after briefly leading, saying Red Bull's lack of energy deployment cost a lot, while pole-sitter Pierre Gasly slipped to seventh for Alpine.
body: Max Verstappen turned fifth on the grid into a podium on Sunday 6 September and even led the Italian Grand Prix for several laps after the restart before both Mercedes swept past. He said Red Bull was too slow on the straights for lack of electrical deployment, forcing late braking and outside passes. Crumbling tarmac at Turn 2 also threw debris into his path. Liam Lawson finished 14th.

Pierre Gasly's fairytale lasted a handful of laps. The Frenchman led from his first career pole at the original start but faded to seventh after the red flag, with Alpine teammate Franco Colapinto ninth. Arvid Lindblad took eighth for Racing Bulls and Yuki Tsunoda the final point. Both Aston Martins retired, Lance Stroll's hydraulics failure triggering the race-deciding Virtual Safety Car.

sports.h3: Canfield's US team snatch SailGP Valencia final as Spain crash out at home
sports.summary: Taylor Canfield's United States crew beat Tom Slingsby's Australians on the final turn to win the Spain Sail Grand Prix in Valencia on Sunday 6 September, while home team Los Gallos missed the final.
body: The Spain Sail Grand Prix in Valencia ended dramatically on Sunday 6 September. Taylor Canfield's United States SailGP Team trailed Australia's Bonds Flying Roos for almost the entire four-boat final, but when the Australians stalled off their foils in a patchy 13 to 14 km/h breeze the Americans grabbed the inside line at the last mark and won by eleven seconds.

The US team collected the 400,000 dollar event prize and climbed from fourth to third in the standings on 56 points, one ahead of Artemis. Red Bull Italy, driven by Phil Robertson, took third for a first event podium. Diego Botin's Spanish Los Gallos finished last in the decisive race on home water. Slingsby's Australians lead on 85 points with three events left, starting in Geneva on 19 September.

sports.h3: Black Foils sink in Valencia as Maxi Yacht Rolex Cup opens in Porto Cervo
sports.summary: Peter Burling's New Zealand crew finished last in their SailGP group in Valencia, while nearly 40 maxis over 60 feet began racing for two world titles at the Maxi Yacht Rolex Cup on Sunday 6 September.
body: It was a weekend to forget for the Black Foils. Peter Burling's New Zealand team finished bottom of Group A after Saturday's six races in Valencia and sit 12th in the SailGP standings on 21 points. The team blamed a lack of light-air time after months lost to February's collision with the French boat in Auckland. Artemis, despite a broken jib halyard, still reached final contention.

In Sardinia, the Maxi Yacht Rolex Cup opened from Porto Cervo on Sunday 6 September. Organised by the Yacht Club Costa Smeralda with the International Maxi Association, it runs until 12 September and doubles as the Rolex IMA Maxi 1 and Maxi Grand Prix World Championships. Close to 40 yachts over 60 feet are entered, with the WallyCento Galateia and Django 7X defending titles.

sports.h3: PSV win first topper of the season 3-1 at Ajax as Van Bommel escapes red
sports.summary: Ricardo Pepi, debutant Lutsharel Geertruida and Esmir Bajraktarevic scored as champions PSV beat Ajax 3-1 in the Johan Cruijff ArenA on Saturday 5 September, leaving Ajax winless at home this season.
body: PSV took just four minutes to lead in Amsterdam on Saturday 5 September, Ricardo Pepi nodding in after Ruben van Bommel headed Ivan Perisic's cross back across goal. Tolu Arokodare levelled for Ajax in the 23rd minute and Steven Berghuis and Davy Klaassen wasted clear chances before debutant Lutsharel Geertruida volleyed PSV back in front with the last kick of the first half.

The second half was marked by an ugly body check from Van Bommel that caught Ajax defender Aaron Bouwman in the face. Referee Sander van der Eijk showed only yellow, sparking a confrontation on the benches. Substitute Esmir Bajraktarevic sealed the 3-1 win in stoppage time. Ajax have gone five home league games without a win and trail PSV by six points with a game in hand.

sports.h3: Feyenoord win 3-1 at NEC without Hadj Moussa ahead of Barcelona test
sports.summary: Gjivai Zechiel scored once and set up two more as Feyenoord beat NEC 3-1 in Nijmegen on Saturday 5 September, with Anis Hadj Moussa left out for turning up late twice.
body: Feyenoord bounced back from their 2-2 draw with ADO Den Haag by winning 3-1 at NEC on Saturday 5 September. After a quiet first half, NEC's Dortmund loanee Almugera Kabar miscontrolled in his own half and Gjivai Zechiel converted Nacho Ferri's assist for his fourth league goal of the season. Darko Nejasmic replied almost immediately with a superb left-footed strike from distance.

Zechiel then set up Luciano Valente for 2-1 just after the hour and debutant Jerayno Schaken added a late third. Coach Giovanni van Bronckhorst left Anis Hadj Moussa at the hotel for disciplinary reasons after the Algerian winger was late twice, amid reported interest from Al-Ittihad. Feyenoord have 11 points from five games and open their Champions League campaign at home to Barcelona on Wednesday.

sports.h3: Keeper Koeman Jr scores twice, Utrecht fans force abandonment, AZ stay top
sports.summary: Telstar goalkeeper Ronald Koeman Jr converted two penalties in a 2-2 draw with Cambuur on Sunday, while FC Utrecht's match against Go Ahead Eagles was suspended after fans threw fireworks and cups.
body: Telstar goalkeeper Ronald Koeman Jr made Eredivisie history on Sunday 6 September as the first keeper to score twice in one league match. Down to ten men after an early red card for Nokkvi Thorisson and trailing 2-0 at newly promoted Cambuur, Telstar won two penalties. Koeman buried the first in the 63rd minute and the second in the 101st. Cambuur stay bottom.

Saturday's game between FC Utrecht and Go Ahead Eagles was abandoned with 25 minutes left after Utrecht fans twice disrupted play, first with fireworks at 3-0 down and then with plastic cups. The remainder is played behind closed doors on Tuesday. AZ kept a perfect record with a 3-2 comeback win at Heerenveen to stay two points clear of PSV. Excelsior won 3-0 at Willem II.

sports.h3: World Master wraps in Las Vegas as ADCC 2026 countdown hits final week
sports.summary: The IBJJF World Master Championship concluded its three-day run in Las Vegas on Saturday 5 September, with attention now turning to the ADCC World Championship in Krakow on 12 and 13 September.
body: The 2026 IBJJF World Master Championship closed on Saturday 5 September after three days at the Las Vegas Convention Center, run alongside the Jiu-Jitsu Con festival. Saturday's final day was headlined by the black belt Master 1 and Master 2 brackets, following Friday's purple and senior black belt divisions. FloGrappling streamed all three days and the IBJJF database carries every bracket.

The grappling calendar now pivots to Krakow, where the ADCC World Championship takes place at Tauron Arena on 12 and 13 September, preceded by the bracket reveal on Friday 11 September. Five men's divisions of 16 and three women's divisions of eight will compete, with Brazil's Micael Galvao favoured to defend his 2024 title. Fight to Win 324 runs on the Saturday night.

sports.h3: Judo heads for Budapest Grand Slam as Baku Worlds loom in October
sports.summary: Continental opens in San Salvador and Podgorica filled the judo weekend of 5 and 6 September, with the Hungary Grand Slam in Budapest from 11 to 13 September the last major before the World Championships in Baku.
body: The IJF World Tour had a quiet weekend on 5 and 6 September, with the action spread across smaller ranking events. A continental open in San Salvador drew 141 judoka from 16 nations, while a second open in Podgorica on Sunday featured 128 athletes from 12 countries. Both were streamed on JudoTV and count towards the 2026 world ranking season.

The next stop is the Hungary Grand Slam in Budapest from 11 to 13 September, with 547 judoka from 71 countries entered. It is the final Grand Slam before the 2026 World Judo Championships in Baku from 4 to 11 October, so most contenders will use it as a last test. Dutch fans will watch the women's -70 kg and -78 kg divisions and the men's +100 kg class.

consumer-tech.h3: Apple's Surprise and Shine event on Wednesday: foldable iPhone Ultra headlines
consumer-tech.summary: Apple holds its September event on Wednesday 9 September at 19:00 Dutch time, with a 2,000 dollar-plus foldable iPhone Ultra, the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max, two Apple Watches and AirPods 5 expected, and new CEO John Ternus hosting for the first time.
body: Apple's biggest launch in years takes place on Wednesday 9 September at 19:00 Dutch time. The headline act is the company's first foldable, tipped to be called iPhone Ultra: a book-style device with a 5.5-inch outer display opening to about 7.8 inches, Touch ID in the side button and a 2nm A20 Pro chip. TrendForce estimates a starting price of 2,099 dollars.

The iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max keep last year's shape but add a variable aperture camera and a smaller Dynamic Island, with prices expected to rise by 100 to 300 dollars. The standard iPhone 18 slips to spring 2027. Also expected: Apple Watch Series 12, Watch Ultra 4 and AirPods 5. It is John Ternus's first keynote as CEO since Tim Cook stepped down.

consumer-tech.h3: IFA 2026 wraps: somersaulting robots, sleep earbuds and a bezel-less phone
consumer-tech.summary: Europe's biggest consumer electronics show ran in Berlin from 4 to 8 September, with TechRadar and Gizmodo handing out best-of awards to Agibot's A3 humanoid, Anker's sleep tech, DJI's new cameras and Tecno's bezel-free concept phone.
body: IFA Berlin, which ran from 4 to 8 September, was one of the stronger editions in years according to outlets that walked the halls. TechRadar's 25 Best in Show picks included the 55 kg Agibot A3 humanoid that can somersault and perform in swarms of up to 100 units, the sub-2,000 dollar Hypershell X Ultra S exoskeleton and JMGO's 4K 120Hz Iris Ultra Max projector.

Gizmodo's awards, published on Saturday 5 September, went to Tecno's working bezel-less concept phone, the Xiaomi 18 Fold, Eufy's 35,000 Pa Omni E35 robot vacuum, Beyerdynamic's 150 dollar Aventho Y headphones with 90 hours of battery and iRobot's Roomba Duo concept, which releases a smaller robot from its head. Robot lawnmowers with edge-trimming arms and plug-in solar batteries for renters were recurring themes.

consumer-tech.h3: Lenovo's Project Swan rolls a 14-inch laptop out to 17 inches sideways
consumer-tech.summary: Lenovo used IFA to show a laptop whose flexible display extends horizontally into a 17-inch ultrawide, alongside a 990 g ThinkBook and a fanless 830 g concept, while Lexar claimed the world's thinnest SSD at 3.8 mm.
body: Lenovo dominated the PC news out of Berlin. Project Swan is a concept 14-inch laptop that hides a flexible panel in its lid and unfurls sideways into a 17-inch ultrawide, a twist on the vertical rollable Lenovo already sells. It also showed the fanless sub-830 g Project AeroBlade and shipped the 990 g ThinkBook 14x Gen 2 with Intel Core 7 Series 3 chips.

Elsewhere, Lexar's Muse SSD tapers from 3.8 mm to 1 mm and ships with a MagSafe sleeve to record 4K ProRes from an iPhone. Belkin introduced 5,000 and 10,000 mAh semi-solid-state power banks it says last three times longer than conventional cells. Acer's Swift Blade 14 claims the lightest laptop title and Alienware showed a 500 Hz tandem OLED. Nvidia RTX Spark laptops arrive in October.

consumer-tech.h3: DJI doubles up: Osmo 360 II shoots 8K60 and Pocket 4P gets a second lens
consumer-tech.summary: DJI's IFA launches included the Osmo 360 II with 8K at 60 fps and replaceable lenses, and the Osmo Pocket 4P, the first dual-lens pocket gimbal camera with a 1-inch sensor and a 60 mm portrait lens.
body: DJI used Berlin to refresh two of its most popular cameras. The Osmo 360 II adds 8K capture at 60 frames per second, a combination rivals still lack, along with better low-light performance and, for the first time, user-replaceable lenses so a scratched dome no longer means a dead camera. Gizmodo named it the best camera of the show.

The Osmo Pocket 4P is billed as the world's first dual-lens pocket gimbal. A 20 mm equivalent f/2.0 main lens sits on a new 1-inch sensor with 17 stops of dynamic range, paired with a 60 mm f/1.8 portrait lens offering 3x optical and up to 12x digital zoom. ActiveTrack can frame up to eight people. DJI also showed the legged Romo 2 robot vacuum, which steps over 4 cm obstacles.

consumer-tech.h3: Circular Ring 3 adds blood pressure and tap-to-pay in a smaller smart ring
consumer-tech.summary: Circular unveiled the Ring 3 in Slim and Pro versions at IFA, with NFC payments, vibration alerts, blood pressure monitoring and 12 days of battery life, features the Oura Ring 5 still lacks.
body: French wearable maker Circular is going after Oura with the Ring 3, shown in Berlin in Slim and Pro versions. Both are smaller than last year's Ring 2 and add two features no mainstream smart ring offers: NFC for contactless payments and a vibration motor for silent alarms. Battery life is quoted at 12 days, up from seven, and the Pro adds blood pressure monitoring.

Sleep tech was a broader theme at IFA 2026. Anker's Soundcore SleepLab Pro is a bedside speaker that uses 60 GHz radar to track heart rate and sleep stages without a wearable or subscription, while its Sleep Earbuds 4 Pro pair in-ear sensors with a case that doubles as a sleep hub. Motorola's Moto Watch Ultra on Wear OS 6 gives Android users another option.

consumer-tech.h3: Google rolls out Gmail Live, Docs Live and Keep Live voice modes
consumer-tech.summary: Gemini-powered spoken conversations arrived in Gmail, Docs and Keep this week for paying Google AI subscribers, letting users triage an inbox, dictate a first draft or dump notes by talking.
body: Google began rolling out the three Live features announced at I/O in May to Android and iOS this week. Gmail Live lets subscribers hold a spoken back-and-forth with their inbox, asking for details and following up without repeating context. It is available in English worldwide to Google AI Plus, Pro and Ultra subscribers. Docs Live casts Gemini as a hands-free co-writer drawing on Gmail, Drive and the web.

Keep Live, currently Android-only, listens to what Google calls audio brain dumps and turns a rambling stream of consciousness into structured notes and lists. The launch is part of a push to make voice the primary way to use Workspace on the move. TechRadar reports Google is also building a Canva-style design tool inside Workspace on its Nano Banana image model.

consumer-tech.h3: Update Chrome now: sixth zero-day of 2026 patched in 152 release
consumer-tech.summary: Google shipped Chrome 152.0.7977.82 for Windows, Mac and Linux fixing 12 flaws, including a V8 type confusion bug tracked as CVE-2026-85046 that is already being exploited in the wild.
body: Google published a security advisory on Thursday 3 September announcing Chrome 152.0.7977.82 and .83 for Windows and Mac and .82 for Linux. The update closes a dozen vulnerabilities, ten rated high severity. The most urgent is CVE-2026-85046, a type confusion bug in the V8 JavaScript engine that lets a remote attacker run code inside the browser sandbox via a crafted page. Google confirms active exploitation.

The flaw was reported by researcher Salvatore Gulizia, who received a 1,000 dollar bounty. It is the sixth Chrome zero-day patched this year. Because the bug sits in V8, every Chromium-based browser is affected, so Edge, Brave, Opera and Vivaldi users should update once their vendors ship fixes. The rollout is staged, so users can force it via Help, then About Google Chrome.

consumer-tech.h3: Windows 11 will switch on memory integrity by default, gamers grumble
consumer-tech.summary: Microsoft is using quality updates to enable memory integrity and Virtualization Based Security on eligible Windows 11 PCs, a move some gamers say costs them frame rates and 1 percent lows.
body: Microsoft has confirmed that upcoming Windows 11 quality updates will automatically turn on memory integrity protection, also known as HVCI, on eligible devices, along with Virtualization Based Security where it is not yet active. The company framed the change as security built in rather than bolted on, hardening kernel-mode drivers. PCs where the feature was deliberately disabled, or managed by group policy, are exempt.

The reaction on Reddit and elsewhere has been split. VBS has long been blamed for gaming slowdowns, and some users report frame rate hits approaching 10 percent and worse stuttering in 1 percent lows even on high-end hardware. Others say the impact on modern platforms is negligible and secure defaults are right for a mass-market OS. TechRadar's Darren Allan sided with Microsoft, provided Windows tells users.

consumer-tech.h3: Tesla Cybercab launches in Austin and lands under NHTSA audit on day one
consumer-tech.summary: Tesla began carrying passengers in its two-seat, steering-wheel-free Cybercab in Austin on Thursday 3 September, the same day US regulators opened an audit into how it self-certified the vehicle. Shares fell 6 percent on Friday.
body: Tesla's long-promised Cybercab entered commercial service in Austin on Thursday 3 September with no livestream, no stage and no remarks from Elon Musk. A small group of shareholders and influencers rode first before the vehicle opened up through the Robotaxi app. The purpose-built two-seater has no steering wheel, pedals or mirrors and runs software closely related to Full Self-Driving.

The same day, NHTSA's Office of Defects Investigation opened Audit Query AQ26002 covering an estimated 1,000 Cybercabs. Because US automakers self-certify compliance, the agency wants the technical basis for Tesla's view that rules written around a human driver do not apply. It sits alongside an FSD probe covering 3.2 million vehicles. Tesla shares fell about 6 percent on Friday 4 September after the launch was judged underwhelming.

consumer-tech.h3: RivianOS 2 unifies R1 and R2 software with Unreal Engine 5 graphics
consumer-tech.summary: Rivian began pushing version 2026.31 to R1 and R2 owners on Friday 4 September, its biggest software overhaul yet, with a rebuilt interface, speed camera alerts and a deeper AI assistant layer.
body: Rivian's RivianOS 2 puts first-generation R1s, second-generation R1s and the new R2 on a single software stack for the first time. The update, numbered 2026.31, started reaching vehicles on Friday 4 September. The R2 and Gen 2 R1 render real-time 3D visualisations of the car in Unreal Engine 5, while Gen 1 trucks stay on Unreal Engine 4. The settings menu gains universal search.

Navigation adds Real-Time Route Alerts that fold police presence and speed-camera data into Google Maps, a clear nod to Waze. A weather app and Mobile Live Trips sit behind the 14.99 dollar a month Connect+ subscription. The Hey Rivian assistant uses hybrid edge compute on newer vehicles for lower latency. Electrek said the update shows why Volkswagen partnered with Rivian on software.

consumer-tech.h3: Norway hits 98.7 percent EV share as BYD posts record 440,293 August sales
consumer-tech.summary: August registration data showed battery electric cars at 98.7 percent of Norway's market, 85.9 percent in Denmark and a record 46.2 percent in Belgium, while BYD's overseas sales jumped 134 percent.
body: Europe's electric transition set fresh records in August. In Norway, battery electric cars took 98.7 percent of new passenger registrations, led by the Volkswagen ID.4 and Toyota bZ4X, with Tesla's Model 3 slipping to seventh. Denmark reached 85.9 percent, Belgium recorded 46.2 percent and Spain's electrified share hit a record 27.7 percent. The Netherlands hovered around 50 percent.

BYD reported 440,293 new energy vehicle sales for August, its best month of 2026, with overseas deliveries up 134 percent year on year. In Germany the brand registered 5,256 cars, a rise of 372 percent, taking its eight-month total to 36,748. BYD and Xpeng together took 11.4 percent of Norway's market. BYD has also launched what it calls its biggest-ever UK sales event.

consumer-tech.h3: Uber and Wayve launch Britain's first autonomous rides in London
consumer-tech.summary: From Thursday 3 September, London Uber riders can be matched with a Ford Mustang Mach-E driven by Wayve's AI at no extra cost, though a licensed safety driver remains behind the wheel for now.
body: Uber and London-based Wayve switched on what they call the UK's first autonomous ride-hailing service on Thursday 3 September. Riders booking UberX, Uber Electric or Uber Comfort anywhere in London except airports may be offered an electric Mustang Mach-E fitted with the Wayve AI Driver. There is no surcharge and passengers can decline. More than 140,000 Londoners had already opted in.

A Transport for London-licensed driver stays behind the wheel ready to take over, so this is not yet a driverless robotaxi in the Waymo sense. Wayve has trained its end-to-end AI on London's roads since 2018. The launch follows Uber's investment in the start-up and a deal covering 12 global markets, with Nissan Leafs due in Tokyo later this year. Fully driverless services await the Automated Vehicles Act.
